page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the high clock speed family, designed for compute-intensive workloads that require predictable processor frequencies. Built on KVM virtualization with dedicated CPU allocation, the instance provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores running on an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor at 3.3 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 for accelerated vector calculations.

The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The memory subsystem demonstrates upper-quartile capabilities, logging a PassMark memory score of 2,865.83 and large-block read throughput of 113.29 GB/sec. The instance lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data operations, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps without bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.hfc7.12xlarge largely in the middle tier of general compute performance, registering a PassMark CPU score of 40,369.24 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,926.0. Parallel decompression demonstrates significant capacity, achieving 206.84 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 tests. In transactional and serving benchmarks, the instance delivers 40.04 million Redis SET operations per second and 27.12 GB/sec static web throughput, while small 135M parameter LLM inference achieves 2,065.05 prompt tokens per second.

With its 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation and reliance on external block storage, the instance favors high-frequency batch execution, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed computational jobs, and scientific simulations over memory-heavy analytics or large-scale in-memory caching platforms.
